name: New Jersey

agency.name: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Division of Workers' Compensation

ttd.rateText: 70% of the average weekly wage, not more than 75% of the Statewide Average Weekly Wage and not less than 20% of the SAWW (Division of Workers' Compensation, Temporary total disability benefits; N.J.S.A. 34:15-12).
ttd.minText: Minimum temporary disability rate for 2026 is $320 (20% of SAWW); permanent partial disability has a separate $35 minimum.

waiting.text: The worker must be unable to work for seven days (including weekends and holidays, not necessarily consecutive) before temporary disability benefits are payable; benefits are then retroactive to the first day. No waiting period applies to medical or permanent disability benefits (Division of Workers' Compensation, Injured Worker FAQ).

ttdDuration.text: TTD is paid while the worker is unable to work and under active medical care; it usually ends on release to work in some capacity or at maximum medical improvement (Division of Workers' Compensation, Temporary total disability benefits).

ppd.text: PPD is a percentage of a 'scheduled' loss (arm 330 weeks, leg 315 weeks, hand 260/300 weeks, eye 200 weeks, etc.) or a 'non-scheduled' loss of the body as a whole based on 600 weeks, paid weekly after temporary disability ends; the weekly PPD rate ranges from a $35 minimum to the $1,199 maximum in 2026 (Schedule of Disabilities effective 1/1/2026; N.J.S.A. 34:15-12(c)).

facts.text: New Jersey's 2026 maximum of $1,199 (up from $1,159) reflects the $1,598.66 statewide average weekly wage for 2024, recalculated each year from the wage two years earlier (NJDOL press release, December 29, 2025).
The employer and its insurance carrier select the treating physicians; a worker who disputes care can file a Motion for Medical and/or Temporary Disability Benefits (N.J.S.A. 34:15-15, Division FAQ).
If the worker recovers from a negligent third party, the employer or carrier generally gets a credit of two-thirds of its compensation payments less $750 (N.J.S.A. 34:15-40, Division FAQ).
The Second Injury Fund pays permanent total benefits when a work injury combines with pre-existing disabilities; the employer pays only the work-related portion (Division of Workers' Compensation).
A formal claim petition must be filed within two years of the injury or the last compensation payment, whichever is later (Division FAQ).

uncertain: N.J.S.A. section text was not read directly (state statute site not reached); section numbers 34:15-12/-14 are cited from the standard structure of the Workers' Compensation Law, while -15 and -40 are cited by the Division's own FAQ.
New Jersey law is commonly described as capping TTD at 400 weeks, but no official page read on 2026-10-08 states the cap, so maxWeeks is null.
